title: How he got to Fletcher Henderson's house
summary: Turner told Thomas he'd soon be with Fletcher Henderson, and the union could scare you. Through Keg Johnson, Thomas rehearsed at Henderson's house.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: But, Charlie always said to me -- I got to tell you this you know -- did you ever meet Charlie? Charlie Turner?
Don't leave out Herman Autrey. I always thought of Joe Louis.

Because he looks like he could fight instead of play the trumpet ... Charlie always said when we got together, he has a place at 155th street, yeah, Fletcher Henderson, get away from me. Well, in those days here's a guy and I'm sure he's the best now. I'm sure he wouldn't mind it and the unions had guys who were knock out guys in those days. They'd scare you. Deprive you of your rights if you went for it but you could a play a one week anywhere in the world, that's what I was told. So, somehow me and Henderson had gotten together, I think it was through Key Johnson.
we had So rehearsal in his house. Fletcher's?
